results.lastReply:
A VPN (virtual private network) is a service that sends your internet traffic through a private, scrambled link before it reaches the website or app you are using. Think of it as a sealed tunnel between your phone or laptop and a company's computer somewhere else.

Because the traffic is scrambled, people on the same Wi-Fi, like in a café or at an airport, can't read what you send. Your internet provider also can't see which sites you visit. The sites see the VPN's address instead of yours, so your location looks different.

A VPN does not make you fully anonymous. The VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust. It also won't protect you from scam links or fake sites.

VPN (virtual private network) ek aisi service hai jo aapka internet use ek private, scrambled raste se bhejti hai, phir wo website tak pahunchta hai. Isse samjho ki aapke phone ya laptop aur VPN company ke computer ke beech ek band suranga hai.

Traffic scrambled hota hai, isliye café ya airport ke Wi-Fi par koi aapka data padh nahi sakta. Aapka internet provider bhi nahi dekh pata ki aap kaun si sites kholte ho. Websites ko aapke address ki jagah VPN ka address dikhta hai, isliye aapki location alag lagti hai.

VPN aapko poori tarah anonymous nahi banata, kyunki VPN company aapka traffic dekh sakti hai. Isliye bharosemand company chuno. Ye aapko scam links ya nakli sites se bhi nahi bachata.
